text:
Last spring the Golden Knights knocked Utah out of the first round in six games. Seven months later the Mammoth are the team pushing play, taking 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), the best share in this matchup by a distance. They have 21 points to show for it, five fewer than Vegas, and the reason has a name. Karel Vejmelka has an .866 save rate and has allowed 7.2 more goals than his shots deserved; over his last five starts he is 1-4 at .847. He gets the start anyway. If you're a Mammoth fan, that's the number you watch all night.

Logan Cooley is the reason to watch Utah regardless. He has 13 points in his last ten games, our numbers say he's earned them, and he already has five career hat tricks, a mark FOX 13 in Salt Lake called NHL history. Clayton Keller has slid onto Barrett Hayton's line with Kailer Yamamoto on injured reserve and has eight assists in a five-game point streak. John Marino is also out, and Mikhail Sergachev is playing 26 minutes a night to cover for it.

Vegas has won three straight, 9-4, on 49% of the chances, with the goaltending saving 6.2 goals more than expected. Adin Hill was the story in Buffalo; Carter Hart starts tonight at .900 with 2.1 goals saved above expected. Trevor Connelly, who won the Detroit game late, has been the find of the road trip. Mitch Marner scored shorthanded on Sunday, and Jack Eichel and Mark Stone are both scoring above their chances. Noah Hanifin and Parker Wotherspoon are out.

Our numbers make it close: Vegas 3.2 expected goals, Utah 3.0. The gap between those two teams' process and results can't hold forever. The question is which side blinks first.
headline: Utah has the chances. Vegas has the goalies.

hunch.text: Utah has been the better team on most nights and has little to show for it. Our gut says this is the night the chances finally go in, even with Vejmelka in net.
